title: SpaceX to begin Starship orbital flights
summary: SpaceX is preparing to initiate orbital flights for its Starship vehicle, with plans to deploy upgraded Starlink satellites on the next mission. The launch is targeted for as soon as the end of the month.

title: Rocket Lab, STR win Space Force contracts for airborne-target tracking
summary: Rocket Lab and Sierra Technical Services (STR) secured $615 million in Space Force contracts for the AMTI satellite program to track airborne targets. The contracts include a third unidentified vendor.

title: Telesat lands $1.63 billion Canadian defense contract
summary: Telesat secured a $1.63 billion Canadian defense contract to expand its Lightspeed LEO satellite network, increasing the planned constellation to 225 spacecraft.

title: NOAA purchases Spire hyperspectral microwave sounder data
summary: NOAA extended a $3 million contract with Spire Global to evaluate data from its Hyperspectral Microwave Sounder (HyMS). The agreement aims to assess the satellite data's utility for weather forecasting and climate research.

title: Rubicon ASCENT thruster moves from hot-fire testing to production
summary: Rubicon Space Systems has completed hot-fire testing of its Velox 5-newton ASCENT monopropellant thruster, transitioning it to production. The thruster is expected to support on-orbit operations by 2027.

title: Military demand shapes market for satellite propulsion
summary: Military demand is driving investment in satellite propulsion systems, enabling small satellites to change orbits more freely. Startups and established manufacturers are focusing on developing these engines.

title: Future of Crew Dragon weighs on commercial spaceflight industry
summary: SpaceX acknowledges significant remaining lifespan for its Crew Dragon fleet but has not committed to its long-term operational future, creating uncertainty in the commercial spaceflight industry.

title: SpaceX’s new Starfall program offers validation and competition for reentry startups
summary: SpaceX launched the first test flight of its Starfall commercial reentry capsule on June 23, validating the demand for microgravity research and manufacturing. The program also introduces competition for other reentry startups in the space industry.

title: Rocketdyne reemerges as standalone space company
summary: Rocketdyne has reemerged as an independent space company after AE Industrial, a private-equity firm, acquired a 60% stake. L3Harris retains a noncontrolling interest in the newly standalone entity.

title: Kreios Space to fly VLEO demonstration in NanoAvionics bus
summary: Kreios Space plans to conduct the first very low Earth orbit (VLEO) demonstration using its air-breathing electric propulsion (ABEP) aboard a NanoAvionics bus. The demonstration is scheduled to fly with Kongsberg's support.

title: SpaceX wants to launch next Starship this month (and catch it, too), Elon Musk says in 1st earnings call since historic IPO
summary: SpaceX plans to launch its next Starship rocket this month, aiming to catch it during the test flight. This follows Elon Musk's remarks in the company's first earnings call since its historic IPO.

title: Watch SpaceX launch 3 giant BlueBird direct-to-cell satellites early on Aug. 5
summary: SpaceX is set to launch three large BlueBird direct-to-cell satellites for AST SpaceMobile on August 5, with the event available to watch live. This mission highlights the growing collaboration between SpaceX and AST SpaceMobile in expanding direct-to-cell satellite services.

title: When a total solar eclipse darkens the sky on Aug. 12, these citizen scientists will be watching
summary: A citizen scientist initiative is preparing to observe the total solar eclipse on August 12. The project aims to engage the public in solar eclipse research.

title: August full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Sturgeon Moon
summary: The Sturgeon Moon, the full moon of August 2026, will peak at a specific time and can be observed with skywatching highlights. The guide provides details on when, where, and how to see it.

title: SpaceX launches Starlink satellites on 90th Falcon 9 flight of the year (video)
summary: SpaceX launched 24 Starlink satellites on Aug. 4, marking the 90th Falcon 9 flight of 2026. This mission continues the rapid deployment of SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation.

title: 'A very busy mission': SpaceX on track to launch 4 astronauts to the ISS on Sept. 12
summary: SpaceX is preparing to launch four astronauts to the International Space Station (ISS) on September 12, with NASA and SpaceX officials confirming readiness during a media briefing on August 3. The Crew-13 mission marks another collaborative effort between NASA and SpaceX.

title: A 9,000-pound SpaceX rocket will crash into the moon tonight. Will you be able to see it?
summary: A 9,000-pound SpaceX rocket is expected to crash into the moon tonight, with a potential plume of debris visible from Earth. The impact itself will likely not be directly observable.

title: ISS astronaut spies a swirling super storm | Space photo of the day for Aug. 4, 2026
summary: NASA astronaut Anil Menon captured a striking photo of a swirling typhoon from the International Space Station on Aug. 2, 2026. The image was featured as the Space Photo of the Day for Aug. 4, 2026.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 4, 2007: NASA launches Phoenix Mars lander to Red Planet
summary: NASA launched the Phoenix Mars Lander on August 4, 2007, to explore the Martian arctic. This mission marked the first landing in the planet's polar region.

title: 'Significant areas of Mars may have once been covered by water': Scientists find hidden clue in Spirit rover data
summary: A new analysis of NASA's Spirit rover data reveals traces of crystalline hematite and altered magnetite, suggesting significant areas of Mars were once covered by water. This discovery supports the theory that liquid water played a major role in shaping the planet's past.

title: Crew-13 pilot reflects on career, training, and upcoming science ahead of flight to ISS
summary: NASA has moved up the next International Space Station (ISS) mission, Crew-13, with a pilot reflecting on their career, training, and upcoming scientific research. The launch, originally planned for November, has been rescheduled earlier.

title: While SpaceX recovers Ship 40, Ship 41 prepares for testing ahead of Flight 14
summary: SpaceX is recovering Ship 40 after its soft landing in the Indian Ocean, while Ship 41 prepares for testing ahead of Flight 14.

title: Launch Preview: Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions fill launch manifest
summary: The first full week of August is expected to be busy with multiple space missions, including launches by Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese space missions. This highlights a busy period for the space industry with several high-profile launches planned.

title: Boeing’s Starliner set for potential 2026 cargo run to ISS
summary: Boeing's CST-100 Starliner spacecraft is undergoing redesign work for a potential cargo mission to the ISS in 2026. Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg highlighted the ongoing modifications.

title: Starbase Pad 1 Retrofits Progress as Block 3 Flights Start
summary: SpaceX has completed two flights from the newly designed Pad 2 at Starbase, while retrofitting work continues on Pad 1. The upgrades are part of preparations for Block 3 flights.

title: Blue Origin continues rebuilding LC-36, prepares testing alternatives for New Glenn second stage
summary: Blue Origin is continuing to rebuild Launch Complex 36 (LC-36) and exploring alternative testing methods for the second stage of its New Glenn rocket following a recent pad explosion during a static fire test.

title: Ship 40’s flawless flight promotes next mission catch potential
summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 13 successfully completed its mission with Ship 40 returning intact, demonstrating flawless performance and paving the way for future missions. The achievement highlights the potential for next mission catch operations.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9 and Chang Zheng rockets set to launch this week
summary: Five orbital launches are scheduled worldwide this week, including a Chang Zheng 6A rocket in China. SpaceX's Falcon 9 is also set to launch.

title: Juno reveals surprising subsurface tempertures at Io, remarkably smooth surface
summary: NASA's Juno mission reveals surprising subsurface temperatures and a remarkably smooth surface on Jupiter's moon Io after two flybys. The findings challenge previous assumptions about the moon's volcanic activity and geology.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to hot-fire test the second stage of the New Glenn rocket at the Stennis B-2 stand. This marks a significant step in preparing the New Glenn rocket for its upcoming missions.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of significant contributions by the European Space Agency.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency's technical center in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will demonstrate formation flying with two satellites to create an artificial solar eclipse for coronagraph observations. The mission aims to study the Sun's corona while the satellites alternately block and reveal Earth in a 'hide and seek' maneuver.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will be held on September 16-17 at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands, bringing together space startups and industry leaders to exchange ideas and collaborate. The event aims to showcase capabilities, discuss partnerships, and explore opportunities within Europe's space sector.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technologies for next-generation antennas. These innovations are expected to enhance communication systems in the space industry.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber, confirming its electronics are fit for space. The mission is scheduled to launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant advancement in environmentally friendly propulsion technology for space missions.

title: Upcoming ESA–Industry events on CM25 implementation
summary: ESA is hosting industry events to present follow-up actions to the CM25 meeting, detailing planned activities and opportunities for industry participation.

title: FL Governor Candidate Launches Space Race Policy
summary: A Florida gubernatorial candidate has unveiled a space race policy to attract launches, investments, and high-paying jobs, aiming to compete with other states and countries.

title: Xona Clears Final Regulatory Hurdle for PNT Constellation
summary: Xona Space Systems has received FCC approval to broadcast Pulsar navigation signals from its full satellite constellation, marking the final regulatory hurdle before scaling deployment.

title: Kreios Taps Kongsberg NanoAvionics for 2028 VLEO Demo
summary: Kreios has selected Kongsberg NanoAvionics to support its 2028 Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) demonstration mission, aiming to validate its ability to operate an Atmospheric-Breathing Electric Propulsion (ABEP) thruster at various altitudes below Low Earth Orbit (LEO).

title: True Anomaly Chases an Evading Target
summary: True Anomaly successfully executed an in-space pursuit of an evading target as part of the VICTUS HAZE mission, marking a first for the company. The achievement demonstrates advancements in space maneuverability and tracking capabilities.

title: AFRL Adds $11.7M to Blue Origin’s Point-to-Point Cargo Contract
summary: Blue Origin received an $11.7M contract increase from AFRL to study point-to-point cargo delivery using its launcher. The additional funding aims to explore the launcher's capabilities for rapid logistics missions.

title: K2 Space Raises $500M Series D at $6.8B Valuation
summary: K2 Space raised $500 million in a Series D funding round, valuing the company at $6.8 billion. This brings K2 Space's total financing to over $1 billion since 2022.

title: NordSpace Funds NVD Amid Canada’s Export Push
summary: NordSpace Ventures invested in North Vector Dynamics, a company developing full-spectrum sovereign missile capability. This move aligns with Canada's push to bolster its export capabilities in the defense sector.

title: Report: Our Launch Cadence Forecast For Next-Gen Rockets
summary: The article discusses the expected flight cadence ramp for next-gen reusable rockets, including New Glenn, Neutron, Nova, Terran R, and Eclipse. It aims to forecast the launch frequency of these advanced rockets.

title: Payload Field Guide: European Launchers
summary: Europe is rapidly developing new launch capabilities but faces challenges in keeping pace with global competitors. The continent's progress in space launch is highlighted despite slower-than-hoped advancements.

title: Hop Aero Wants to Deliver Cargo via Rocket
summary: Hop Aero, a startup, introduced its autonomous suborbital rocket, Rook, through Y Combinator. The company aims to deliver cargo using this rocket technology.

title: L3Harris Confirms Successful Deployment for First Perimeter Truss Reflector on ViaSat-3
summary: L3Harris Technologies successfully deployed its first perimeter truss reflector onboard the ViaSat-3 Flight 3 satellite. The satellite was launched by SpaceX in late April as part of Viasat's third deployment.

title: Kreios Space to Demo Air-breathing Electric Propulsion in VLEO With NanoAvionics
summary: Kreios Space will demonstrate an air-breathing electric propulsion (ABEP) system in Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) using a spacecraft bus provided by Kongsberg NanoAvionics. The Spanish satellite startup aims to showcase this innovative propulsion technology for future space missions.

title: Telesat Expands Lightspeed Constellation for Arctic Military Satcom Program
summary: Telesat secured a $1.9 billion contract with the Canadian government to expand its Lightspeed constellation by 69 satellites for Arctic military satcom connectivity. The deal aims to enhance secure communications in the Arctic region.

title: Endeavor Optical Networks Emerges From Stealth to Build Optical MEO Data Transfer
summary: Endeavor Optical Networks has come out of stealth mode to develop an optical satellite network in Medium-Earth Orbit (MEO) for space-based data transfer. The startup aims to enhance high-speed data connectivity using optical communication technology.

title: Airbus and Thales Alenia Space to Build SpainSat NG-III
summary: Airbus and Thales Alenia Space have been contracted by Hisdesat to build the SpainSat NG-III secure satellite communications satellite for Spain. Airbus will serve as the prime contractor for the project.

title: ETL Acquires Software Developer Amphinicy Technologies
summary: ETL Systems has acquired Amphinicy Technologies, a software developer specializing in satcom and Earth Observation markets. The acquisition aims to enhance ETL's ability to address complex ground segment challenges.

title: Xona Gets Approval to Deploy Commercial Navigation Constellation
summary: Xona has received FCC approval to deploy its commercial navigation constellation called Pulsar, which is planned to consist of more than 250 satellites. The company announced the authorization to broadcast radionavigation signals.

title: Hughes Files for Chapter 11 With Plan to Reorganize Around Enterprise, Defense Business
summary: Hughes Satellite Systems Corporation filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection to reorganize around enterprise, defense, and government customers due to a decline in consumer business.

title: AccelerCom and Eclipse Space Reveals Details of D2D Collaboration
summary: AccelerComm and Eclipse Space have announced a collaboration to define the physical-layer architecture for Eclipse's next-generation Direct-to-Device (D2D) spacecraft. AccelerComm completed two engineering engagements to support Eclipse's sovereign satellite infrastructure development.

title: K2 Space Secures Series D Funding After Hitting $1 Billion Contract Value Milestone
summary: K2 Space raised $500 million in a Series D funding round, valuing the company at nearly $7 billion. This follows the company surpassing $1 billion in contract value milestones.
